requiredness.declared_in: producer_rules_v1.js (the rules module the validator is bound to)
requiredness.enforced_by: validateDmObservation → error DM_OBSERVATION_BLOCK_REQUIRED (ERROR, never a warning)
requiredness.★_semantics: ★ A MISSING dm_designed_detail_evidence block is NOT "no designed detail". Missing = we do not know whether DM observation was performed. When nothing is admitted the block is emitted explicitly with evidence: []. Conflating the two would let a model that silently skipped the DM task validate as a clean garment.
requiredness.★_version_scoped_by_construction: ★ The flag lives in the bound rules module. The sealed Producer V1 and V1_1 do not define it, so their behaviour is untouched. ⛔ No directory-name test, no glob, no "latest" lookup, no environment-dependent routing.
requiredness.⛔_separate_from_completeness: ⛔ This is a SECOND, independent gate. The 37-parameter completeness gate is unchanged and the two are never summed — DM requiredness is not implemented as 38/38.
requiredness.legacy_mode: ★ CORRECTED 2026-09-10 — NONE. This field previously read "validateDmObservation(target, { requireDmObservation: false }) preserves pre-correction behaviour". That runtime bypass was REMOVED by the Integration Closure order §7 and the line was left behind stale. There is no caller-side way to switch requiredness off on this line: it is read only from the bound rules module and is hard fail-closed. Legacy behaviour is verified by loading the REAL V1 / V1_1 validators, never by degrading this one.

dm_observation_layer.★_m1_eligible_families_meaning_as_of_v1_: the frozen M1 CALIBRATION fact consumed by the engine-side M1 predicate — no longer a container gate
dm_observation_layer.★_direction_bounded_support_consumer: dm_direction_resolver_v1.js reads the two realization fields as raw observation at the moderate-separation boundary (CEO scope amendment 2026-09-10). It never reads an M1 verdict and never branches on family.
